issues.body: At `term_to_ntriples`, the `bnode` arm still appends `term.value` directly after `_:` without validating blank-node-label grammar. The catch-all arm still accepts `kind: "triple"` and unknown kinds alike, and when `triple` is absent returns attacker-controlled `term.value` verbatim. Because `TermRef` remains public and deserializable, either path can inject executable syntax into DELETE/INSERT output. Structured triples do not close the opaque fallback, and the added malicious-deserialization test exercises only literal language/direction metadata.
issues.fix_hint: Match only the four explicit kinds and reject unknown kinds. For `triple`, require structured components and recursively serialize them, or parse and validate the carried text as exactly one RDF triple term before canonical re-emission; never copy opaque text. Validate blank-node labels against the applicable N-Triples grammar. Add positive-control-backed malicious deserialization tests for an opaque triple value, an unknown kind, and a punctuation-bearing blank-node label, each asserting that no update is emitted.
issues.title: Unvalidated term kinds and blank-node labels still permit SPARQL injection

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant. The round-3 major injection finding remains materially unchanged: `term_to_ntriples` still emits blank-node labels verbatim and still treats every non-IRI/non-bnode/non-literal kind as a triple-like fallback, copying `term.value` verbatim when structured components are absent. The new metadata test covers only language/direction payloads and provides no regression coverage for the previously reported opaque triple, unknown-kind, or malicious blank-node cases.
